To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the photo-electron density can be so high that the photo-electrons interact substantially even after ionization and (ii) these interactions can be described by an analytic expression which is based on a sum of synthetic two-body Couloumb collisions.

we have identified a new mechanism of light-matter-interaction, namely the massively parallel ionization of atomic systems, and that we have developed a new theoretical model which describes this new phenomenon and which can be applied to a large variety of systems.
we have found a new phenomenon in strong field physics and that we have proposed an experiment to observe it.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new method for the generation of highly charged ion beams.
the development of a new method to study electron-electron interactions in extended atomic systems by means of a novel type of photo-electron spectroscopy.
the interaction of intense X-ray pulses with extended atomic systems such as clusters and biomolecules.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
massively parallel ionization is a new phenomenon which is not described by the standard theories of photo-ionization.

the photoelectron spectra of extended systems illuminated by intense short XUV pulses are not only determined by single particle dynamics but that the interaction of the electrons with the Coulomb field of the target and among each other plays a crucial role.
this phenomenon can be used to probe the Coulomb dynamics of many-body quantum systems in a unique way.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ionization of many-body systems by intense FEL pulses is a new phenomenon that can be observed in the laboratory.
the ionization dynamics of extended systems becomes a new research topic in the field of ultrafast electron dynamics.
the electron dynamics in the photoionization of extended atomic targets is a many-body problem and that the many-body effects are observable.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the photo-electron spectrum is a fingerprint of the electron-electron interaction and can thus be used to probe the dynamics of many-body systems in the strong-field regime.
the electron-electron interaction in a dense photoelectron gas can be treated as a perturbation.
the electron-electron interactions in the target can be used to extract information about the electron density and the electron distribution function.
